Have you heard of a cell company that doesn't keep any of your data? You might be interested in that too it's an american company I just don't remember the name now.

Maybe Republic Wireless? they are low cost and rely on 3G/4G and Wifi hybrid calling and texting. But it isn't a FOSS phone. As it stand right now, if one does not have Orbot and / or an encrypted SD Card in their phone, the Blackberry is king of secure phones.

 

Privacy, however, is dependent not only on the hardware maker of the phone, but also if the apps downloaded to that phone does not track or enabled information to leak from that app or piece of hardware. This only from my limited knowledge of researching a FOSS-only phone (which for android -- stopped with the APK of Android 2.3.3.)

Unless you root your Republic phone (and potentially bricking it so far as Republic is concerned) you're going to be stuck with a bunch of Google software at the least. I have been using them for a couple of years because of how inexpensive their service is. It's not perfect, but I get more than my money's worth from them. That being said, I know full well that, at the very least, Google has at least some access to a lot of my information, and there's not much I can do about it. At present it's a price I'm willing to grudgingly pay. If a cost competetive alternative came onto the market that was more privacy oriented I'd be more than willing to jump ship, though.
